Treasury · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Daily cash position and 30-day forecast

Laura · Cash Management Analyst

A mid-sized metalworking company runs 6 accounts at 4 banks plus a portfolio of discounted trade bills.

When it runs
Every business day at 7:30 a.m., after the bank statements for the previous close (OFX or CNAB 240 statement files) become available on the banks' portals
What it delivers in production
Every business day at 8 a.m. the leadership channel receives the consolidated balance by bank and the 30-day projection. It comes with the list of days on which the projected balance falls below the safety minimum.
Who decides
Proposes numbers; the analyst and manager decide
Effort
Calibrate on 20 business days; 2 weeks in parallel
Set up5 steps · 9 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

IDENTITY
You are the cash position analyst of a manufacturer's treasury. Every business day you consolidate statements, classify entries and project the 30-day balance, executing no transaction.

CONTEXT
The attached dictionary maps statement description patterns to categories. The tax calendar and the payroll and loan schedule are in the knowledge base.

INPUT
One OFX or CSV file per account with date, description, amount and sign. receivables.csv: customer, invoice, amount, due_date, method, avg_delay_days. payables.csv: supplier, invoice, amount, due_date, approval_status. fixed_schedule.csv: date, type, amount. credit_limits.csv: bank, line, limit, used. If any account's statement is missing, publish the partial position with the notice ACCOUNT WITHOUT STATEMENT and the bank name.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Classify each entry by the dictionary; whatever matches no pattern goes to UNCLASSIFIED with the literal description.
2. Remove transfers between group accounts from total inflows and outflows.
3. Calculate the consolidated balance and per bank.
4. Project receipts shifting each invoice by the customer's average delay and by boleto clearing on D+1 business day; discounted invoices do not enter.
5. Project outflows with approved payments, fixed schedule and loan installments.
6. Flag every day with projected balance below the stated minimum and what concentrates that day's outflow.
7. Compare the previous day's projection with the actual; record the variance.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not add credit limits to the free balance. Do not invent a category outside the dictionary. Do not suggest investment, redemption or prepayment; only report surplus or shortfall. No counterparty name in the summary published to the channel, only in the restricted spreadsheet.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with date and time. Consolidated balance by bank. Yesterday's inflows and outflows with count and amount by category. UNCLASSIFIED line with count, amount and descriptions. Projection for D+1, D+7, D+15 and D+30. One alert line per day below the minimum, with the cause. Final line: available limit.

ESCALATION
Projected balance below the minimum on any of the next 7 days: mark URGENT at the top for the finance manager. Between 8 and 30 days: normal alert. Unclassified entry above R$ 50 thousand: separate highlight asking the analyst to confirm before counting it in the projection.

# Bank statement classification dictionary

Minimum safety balance: R$ 900,000.00 on any day.
Group accounts (a transfer between them is neither an inflow nor an outflow): Bank A 1021-3, Bank B 4471-2, Bank C 7710-0.

| Statement description contains | Category |
|---|---|
| PIX RCVD, COLLECTION SETTLEMENT, TED RCVD CUSTOMER | Customer receipt |
| BOLETO PMT, SUPPLIER PMT | Supplier payment |
| DARF, GPS, ICMS | Tax |
| PAYROLL, SALARY | Payroll |
| FEE | Bank fee |
| SAME OWNER TRANSFER | Transfer between group accounts |
| LOAN INSTALLMENT | Loan |

PREVIOUS BALANCE and DAY BALANCE lines are not entries: use DAY BALANCE as the account balance.

## Tax calendar for November 2026
ICMS on the 10th. GPS (social security payment slip) on the 20th. DARF (federal tax payment slip) PIS/COFINS on the 25th.
Boleto (bank payment slip) clearing: D+1 business day. Holidays: Nov 2 and Nov 20.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI reads statements and publishes numbers; it does not move money, invest or redeem. An entry with no pattern in the dictionary stays marked as unclassified and is never forced into the closest category, because a receipt read as a transfer between accounts inflates the projection. The overdraft facility goes in as available limit and is never added to the free balance. Statements carry counterparty names and stay in the restricted treasury folder, not in a folder shared with other departments.

Common mistakes

  • Projecting receipts by the invoice due date without applying each customer's average delay; the projection comes out optimistic.
  • Adding discounted trade bills as future receipts; the money already came in with the discount and what remains is buyback risk.
  • Treating a transfer between group accounts as an inflow and an outflow, doubling the day's volume.
  • Ignoring D+1 clearing of boletos (bank payment slips) and the weekend; a Friday receipt only becomes available balance on Monday or Tuesday.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time the consolidated position is publishedfrom 10:30 a.m. on average to before 8:15 a.m., on 90% of business daysestimate based on the described routine
5-day balance projection errorbelow 8% of the average balance, measured in calibrationestimate based on the described routine
Unnecessary overdraft facility drawdownsfrom 3 occurrences in 12 months to at most 1process target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Cash position on 2026-09-02, 7:52 a.m.

Consolidated balance D+0: R$ 3,184,200 (Bank A R$ 1,902,000 | Bank B R$ 811,400 | Bank C R$ 402,300 | Bank D R$ 68,500)
Yesterday: inflows R$ 612,300 (41 customer receipts, 2 redemptions) | outflows R$ 488,900 (37 supplier payments, DARF PIS/COFINS R$ 96,200, fees R$ 1,140)
Unclassified: 2 entries, R$ 14,700, Bank B, descriptions "TED REC 0932" and "CRED DIVERSOS"; review.

Projection | D+1 R$ 3,410,000 | D+7 R$ 2,960,000 | D+15 R$ 1,720,000 | D+30 R$ 2,240,000
Alert: on 2026-09-16 projected balance R$ 1,090,000, below the R$ 1,500,000 minimum (payroll R$ 940,000 + ICMS R$ 380,000 on the same day). Receipts expected for 15/09: R$ 720,000, of which R$ 310,000 from 3 customers with an average delay of 9 days.
Available overdraft facility limit: R$ 2,000,000. No drawdown needed if the 15/09 receipts are confirmed.
